extracted.intended_audience: state militia/National Guard officers, governors, War Department disbursing/accounting officers, and legal advisors dealing with militia appropriations and property
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of legal decisions and administrative interpretations governing (1) what militia-related expenses and property transactions may be charged to federal militia appropriations (sec. 1661 et seq.), and (2) pay, accounting, custody, and disposition rules for property and personnel of the Organized Militia/National Guard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsistence of enlisted men at prior matches
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance at the prior matches the subsistence of the enlisted men will be defrayed from the funds accruing to the State under its apportionment under section 1661, R. S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioned officers must subsist themselves from their pay as do regular officers. (C. 14148-G, Aug. 19 and 20, 1909.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve militia not eligible for National Guard benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization classed as reserve militia and not part of the State National Guard does not receive funds from the State's apportionment under section 1661, R. S., and service in that organization does not count as service in the National Guard for eligibility to serve on State rifle teams at national matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pay/transportation/subsistence for spectators
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers permitted as spectators to accompany a State team to a national match are not entitled to transportation, pay and subsistence from the appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'year' for pre-allotment participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the requirement that every company/troop/battery participate in practice/inspections during the year next preceding each annual allotment of funds, the word 'year' refers to a calendar year and not a fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 18 of the act of Jan. 21, 1903 (32 Stat. 778) interpreted. C. 14148, May 20, 1903.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation of target supplies chargeable to militia appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of transportation (freight) of target supplies from the State arsenal to the different rifle ranges in the State is a proper charge against the appropriation for promotion of rifle practice (sec. 1661 as amended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes authority to pay for storage of equipment pending lease completion and dray charges from storage to installation site. C. 14148-F, Apr. 16, 1909; C. 14148-C, Feb. 9, 1907.

rubrics_metrics.name: New material transport borne by United States; return transport not
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of transporting new material and supplies issued by staff departments to the Organized Militia will be borne by the United States and paid out of 'Transportation of the Army.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But return transportation from State armories to U.S. depots and arsenals cannot be paid from 'Transportation of the Army.' Articles rendered unserviceable by fair wear and tear must be transported at the cost of the State to which issued. Repairs due to unavoidable accident or fair wear and tear cannot be differentiated from neglect when determining payment of transportation. (Cited decisions: various; see C. 14148-G; Dec. 4, 1906; Apr. 18, 1907; Mar. 24, 1908; Jan. 5, 1909; May 6, 1910; 11055, Feb. 21, 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenses of Organized Militia in joint encampment not payable from Regular Army funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of Apr. 23, 1904 forbids payment of any expenses of the Organized Militia in joint encampment with the Regular Army out of funds appropriated for the Regular Army; expenditure of funds for militia participation is limited to period from leaving home rendezvous to return thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore a State cannot be reimbursed for freight on blankets and ponchos shipped from the State arsenal to company stations as part of equipment for movement to camp of instruction. C. 14148-C, Feb. 15, 1907.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel of militia under War Department orders treated as U.S. troop travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel of militia (e.g., rifle teams) under orders of the War Department, with arrangements made by territorial/state authorities and charged against pro rata allotment, is travel 'as troops of the United States' and subject to laws relating to transportation of U.S. troops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transportation rate not to exceed 50% of Government transportation over 50% land-grant lines; entitled to bond-aided deductions over certain lines. Decision for Hawaii rifle team applies to other States. (C. 19798, Aug., 1907; C. 14148-G, May 10, 1910; others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel payment restrictions for militia same as for U.S. troops
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment under the act of Mar. 23, 1910 for travel of militia required by War Department orders should be governed by the same restrictions that apply to transportation of U.S. troops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection travel by armament foreman chargeable to militia funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Spring inspection travel of militia batteries required for an armament foreman of a district is a lawful charge against the funds accruing to the State under section 1661 and section 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal support vs State responsibility for armory facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress intended to provide arms, armament, clothing, and equipment necessary to prepare militia for active service, while leaving armory facilities and current expenses (and preservation/security of armament) to the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, installation costs for wall lockers in barracks to preserve arms should be paid by the State, not the United States; wall lockers cannot be supplied under section 3 of the act of June 22, 1906. C. 11083, Aug. 22, 1901; C. 14148-C, May 23, 1907.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of State armories by aliens discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing associations of aliens to use State armories for drill is viewed with disfavor because such association might lead to violations of neutrality laws; Department of State should advise State authorities of possible consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blank forms/books are 'supplies' and subject to issue/sale to States
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank forms and blank books prescribed for Army use are 'supplies' under section 17 of Jan. 21, 1903 and may be issued or sold to State authorities for militia use; printing expenses may be charged to the State's allotment under sec. 1661.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cashbooks can be issued as part of State disbursing officer's equipment. Issue of clothing in stock to a State upon proper requisition is mandatory provided the State's allotment balance reimburses cost. C. 14148-C/ -B/ -F etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal Corps field equipment may be furnished to States without cost with accounting adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Fire-control or similar equipment issued by the Signal Corps to Army field batteries may be furnished without cost to States by the Signal Corps through the Ordnance Department, with reimbursement/accounting made by transfers from balances of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits accounting on one set of returns to the Ordnance Department. C. 14148-G, Feb. 2, 1911.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War's armament exceptions for National Guard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the May 27, 1908 amendment, the Secretary of War may authorize general exceptions so that a Field Artillery battalion with complete personal equipment but only sufficient Field Artillery material to fully equip one battery may still be held to conform to the requirement to have the same armament as the Regular Army.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 17 property accounting and sales restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All stores procured and issued to the Army by supply departments fall within operation of section 1661 and sec. 17 for ownership and accounting; such property must be accounted for under specified acts, and sales authorized thereunder are to States only (not individuals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for purchase should be signed by the governor or representative; governor may vest receipt signing in a State Militia officer. Sales to States only, not for other purposes (e.g., flags for capitol not authorized). Trunk lockers and certain items may be sold to States. Horses (battery, cavalry, artillery) cannot be issued or sold to a State under section 17. C. 14148-B and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales to States limited to use of the militia
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales made to States under militia statutes are discretionary with the Secretary of War and must be for the use of the militia; no authority exists for sales to States for other purposes (e.g., state police or capitol flags).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rifle model used by Army may be sold to rifle clubs to promote rifle practice under March 3, 1905 authority, subject to Secretary's regulations. C. 15286; C. 14148-B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans of War Department property generally prohibited absent Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for loan of tents, flags and other public property under War Department control have generally been denied because the Secretary of War lacks authority to loan personal Government property unless authorized by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are rare (e.g., certain dredges). Government ambulances and United States horses cannot be loaned to National Guard in absence of congressional authority. C. 1561, 2265, 14148-E, 10655, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: No relief from accountability by Secretary of War; insurance exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War has no authority to relieve a governor of accountability for supplies receipted for by him even if subsequently lost/destroyed/stolen; Congress alone can grant such relief. If loss is covered by insurance, insurance money may be applied to purchase replacement stores under statutory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 13419; C. 10795. Incidental rental acquisitions for target ranges need not be annually accounted for by governor but reported via vouchers approved by Secretary of War. Section 4 of June 22, 1906 provides settlement methods for unaccounted property as of approval date. No executive disposal of personal property without legislation. C. 14148-B/C, 11054, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repairs to ambulances chargeable to State allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of repairs to ambulances issued to a State for its Organized Militia constitutes a proper charge against the State's allotment under sec. 1661 as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery actions for property issued to States to be instituted in State courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal proceedings to recover arms or other property issued to a State for its Organized Militia should be instituted in State courts, which have original jurisdiction, because custody and possession are in the State though ultimate ownership is in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of condemned clothing and transfer for charitable use
rubrics_metrics.description: Condemned clothing of the National Guard may be placed in custody of trustees (e.g., National School for Boys) for authorized use provided a satisfactory undertaking to destroy after use is received; Secretary of War may, if satisfied clothing will relieve suffering, treat transfer to Associated Charities as equivalent to destruction and modify inspector recommendations accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, fire-control systems damaged by fire should be acted upon by a surveying officer. C. 14148-F; 25978; 14148-H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may act as surveying officer under section 4 (June 22, 1906)
rubrics_metrics.description: Property furnished to States that is lost/destroyed/becomes unserviceable must be examined by a disinterested surveying officer of the Organized Militia; Regular Army officers on duty with Organized Militia may not be ordered to act as surveying officers, nor may retired Regular officers on duty unless they hold a commission as an officer of the Organized Militia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates vs affidavits for boards of survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of certificates in property accountability matters has been restricted to Army officers (based in part on oath of office); officers of the Organized Militia do not take that oath and are not subject to Articles of War. Therefore affidavits, rather than certificates, should be required to support boards of survey findings regarding loss/damage to public property issued to States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An oath to loss/damage can be administered only by one expressly authorized by law. C. 17099; 17265; 18026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of quartermaster supplies retained by U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Army appropriation proviso of May 26, 1900, the Secretary of War is authorized, on application of a governor, to replace quartermaster supplies that volunteers carried into U.S. service and which have been retained by the United States; applies to stores furnished under annual militia appropriation and supplies purchased by States; authorizes replacement article-for-article but not necessarily new articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unexpended balances of permanent militia appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Balances of the permanent appropriation for providing arms and equipments for the militia (sec. 1661) remaining unexpended on June 30 may be used subsequently (e.g., in December) to pay contractors under contracts properly incurred in that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 3690 R.S. exception for 'permanent or indefinite appropriations.' B. 31, 85, Dec, 1870.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement and requisition rules under section 14 of Jan. 21, 1903
rubrics_metrics.description: Moneys drawn from the Treasury under section 14 are to be disbursed under the direction of the governor for payment, subsistence, or transportation and accounted for according to rules for War Department disbursing officers; funds can only be turned over to a State/Territory on a requisition made by the governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A State adjutant general's payment from personal funds does not constitute a payment under the law or prevent payment by the disbursing officer. C. 14148, June 10, 1908; 14148-A, Aug. 25, 1905; 14148-H, Jan. 19, 1911.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War not required to inspect governors' disbursing officers' accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act of Apr. 20, 1874, the Secretary of War is not required to cause the accounts of disbursing officers appointed by governors to be inspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk hire for disbursing officers not chargeable to allotment
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of restrictions on the expenditure of money appropriated for the Organized Militia, clerk hire for disbursing officers does not constitute an expenditure properly chargeable to the State's allotment under the cited acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial status under militia acts (Hawaii example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hawaii's status is that of a Territory within meaning of the militia act of Feb. 12, 1887, and a proportion of the annual militia appropriation shall be apportioned to Territories and D.C. as President prescribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may hire horses under its allotment; related veterinary costs chargeable
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may, under its allotment under sec. 1661, hire horses for its National Guard (including necessary horses for mounted officers); cost of veterinary attention and care for such hired horses is a charge against the allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia allotment funds cannot pay caretakers of U.S. property in Guard custody
rubrics_metrics.description: Money appropriated under section 1661, R.S., as amended, cannot be used to pay caretakers of United States property in the custody of the National Guard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjutant general entitled to pay for authorized field/camp service
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjutant general of a State is an officer of the Organized Militia and if he takes part in actual field or camp service for instruction by order of the governor, he is entitled to pay under section 14; if properly detailed by Secretary of War and participates in joint maneuvers he is also entitled to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heads of staff departments entitled to pay when ordered to camps by governor
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 14, the governor has discretion to order heads of staff departments to take part in a camp of instruction; those officers while so engaged are entitled to pay as provided by that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only officers of authorized participating organizations are payable
rubrics_metrics.description: When organizations of the Organized Militia are authorized by the Secretary of War to participate in an encampment with the Regular Army, no officers other than those belonging to the authorized organizations may be paid by the United States for services rendered during the encampment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursing officer entitled to pay only if selected from participating forces
rubrics_metrics.description: If a disbursing officer is selected from among those who, by governor's orders, are part of forces engaging in camp/field service, he is entitled to pay under section 14; otherwise he is not. He is also entitled to pay for up to 10 days necessarily engaged after return in preparing accounts; a disbursing officer who is not a member of the militia and not actively participating is not eligible for pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 14148, Oct. 1903; Oct. 20, 1903; Sept. 9, 1904. See related Comp. Dec. refs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant surgeon rank/pay while engaged in militia service
rubrics_metrics.description: An assistant surgeon of a State National Guard has rank of captain (by appointment or by operation of law after 5 years) and is entitled while engaged in services specified in sections 14 or 15 to the pay of captain.

rubrics_metrics.name: No special pay maneuvers for enlisted/hire-of-horses workaround
rubrics_metrics.description: A disbursing officer cannot legally pay enlisted men at a different rate of pay than Regular Army rates for the purpose of covering hire of horses. Officers below grade of major whose duty requires them to be mounted and who provide mounts themselves are entitled to the same extra pay as Regular Army officers would be; if the State furnishes a mount from hired horses, the officer is not entitled to extra pay. No law authorizes full reimbursement to militia officers who provided mounts at personal expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: No increased pay for National Guard officers due to length of service or Regular Army longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the National Guard is not entitled to increased pay for length of service when the service was rendered as a commissioned officer of the Organized Militia; officers of the Organized Militia are not entitled to longevity pay because of previous Regular Army service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for officers on special duties related to encampment/reception of troops
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer ordered by the governor to a campground to prepare reception of troops and who submits accounts with muster and pay rolls as required may have the charge paid from funds allotted under sec. 1661.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for service on boards assessing damages during maneuvers
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the National Guard serving on a board to assess damages resulting from joint maneuvers is entitled to the pay and allowances of his rank while his organization remains on duty and until the board completes its labors; compensation charged to the Army appropriation (specific item cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: No pay while on leave during encampment
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer on duty at an encampment is not entitled to pay while on leave under proper orders for a portion of the encampment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retired militia officers not entitled to pay absent recommissioning
rubrics_metrics.description: A retired officer of the militia placed on active duty in connection with camps of instruction, small-arms competition, etc., without being recommissioned on the active list in the Organized Militia, will not be entitled to pay under section 15.
